newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Futures trading arrest by ASC in Sydney.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Futures trading arrest by ASC in Sydney.

text.p: The Australian Securities Commission (ASC) said it arrested Susan Margaret Bahr at Sydney airport on Thursday in relation to six charges of aiding and abetting another officer of Fay Richwhite Futures Australia Ltd.
Bahr appeared before a magistrate at Central Local Court charged with assisting with trading on a client account without the authority of the company or the directors, the ASC said in a statement.
The ASC has alleged that the trading in futures resulted in significant profit and losses of British pounds, yen, deutschmarks and French francs, it said.
The matter was stood over until January 20, it said.
ASC investigations officer Allen Turton told Reuters that Bahr was arrested after attempting to enter Australia from Britain and was picked up through the alert systems at the airport.
Bahr was a back-office employee, he said.
"We sincerely hope so," Turton said when asked if further arrests might take place in relation to the matter.
There was one more co-offender in the case who was not presently in Australia, he said.
Turton could not disclose the person's name or the person's present whereabouts.
A bottom-line figure was not immediately available for release on funds involved in the case, although the amounts of money involved were substantial, he said.
Warrants for Bahr and the co-offender were taken out in late 1994 or early 1995, he said.
